# Allium: formal domain-level specification language for software behavior

Curated by Skill Harbor — @juxt's Allium, a formal language for capturing software behavior at the domain level, sitting between informal feature descriptions and implementation. Describe what software does without prescribing how it's built: entities with fields, enums and state-dependent presence; rules with triggers (state transitions, temporal, entity creation, chained); surfaces defining boundary contracts (facing, exposes, provides, guarantees); contracts and invariants; modular specs referenced by immutable coordinates. The skill teaches the agent the full convergence loop — gather context, take action, verify, repeat — driving the three artifacts (spec, tests, code) to agreement with strict rules: never weaken a generated test to make it pass, escalate genuine ambiguity to the human. A routing table maps tasks to companion skills (elicit, distill, tend, weed, propagate, witness) not included here; `/allium` is the entry point for driving a goal end to end. Honest caveats: this is the language skill only — the companion skills (elicit, distill, weed, propagate, witness) and the `allium` CLI are not included, and you'll be learning a bespoke specification language; an optional hook validates `.allium` files when the CLI is installed. MIT-licensed. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Discovered via skills.sh.
